falsifier: with both frameworks selected, the #1570 page order completes fewer STRIDE findings at 5 or 10 choices than the question turn order
hypothesis: the first-run page of #1570, which shows each group of a round in one box in the order each group first appears, completes as many STRIDE findings at 10 choices with both frameworks selected as the question turn order of E32 (written after the run)
intervention: Offline, run.py early-policies over evals/ at 5b9aa3a2 with box-orders.patch applied (box_orders.py runs the policies with each report's rounds built once): 186 STRIDE reports (2,796 conditional findings) and 31 ASVS reports (4,520 units) on 11 cases. grouped-rounds takes the shipped rounds and shows each in boxes in first-appearance order, as first_run.js after #1570. Both frameworks selected, at 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30 choices. STRIDE completed findings: question turn order 1,009 / 1,147 / 1,168 / 1,293 / 1,865; grouped 52 / 103 / 538 / 1,293 / 1,760. Critical or high: 591 / 658 / 670 / 704 / 961 against 41 / 64 / 325 / 704 / 891. ASVS settled units: 173 / 902 / 1,507 / 1,806 / 1,930 against 864 / 1,489 / 1,806 / 1,806 / 2,027. At 10 choices the grouped order completes no STRIDE finding in 10 of 11 cases. One framework selected: STRIDE alone 946 / 1,488 against 993 / 1,527 at 5 / 10; ASVS alone the same in both orders. The cause: every capability question is in one group, so the first capability question pulls the whole capability box to the top of the round.

signature: a job that selects STRIDE and ASVS asks the ASVS capability questions first, and STRIDE completes no finding in the owner's first choices
